environment.description: Same application deployed on AWS ECS Fargate behind an ALB. The ALB has an associated AWS WAFv2 WebACL with a custom rule group (priority 1) containing a rate-based rule scoped to IP (threshold 100 requests/5min) AND a label-matching rule that inspects the Referer and Origin headers. Specifically, a regex pattern set matches cross-origin POST requests where the Origin header does not match the configured domain allowlist (^https://app\.example\.com$). The rule action is BLOCK with a 403 response for any POST to /api/* paths where Origin does not match. Additionally, the WebACL includes AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet with CrossSiteScripting_BODY and SizeRestrictions_BODY rules in COUNT mode (not block), and a separate custom rule (priority 0) that blocks requests with missing or non-matching Origin/Referer for state-changing methods (POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH) on all /api/* URI paths. The block rule uses a compound statement: (HttpMethod IN [POST,PUT,DELETE,PATCH]) AND (UriPath starts_with /api/) AND NOT (Header:Origin matches regex ^https://app\.example\.com$). This effectively implements origin validation at the WAF layer before requests reach the application.

config.waf_rule_priority_0: Custom rule: Block if (Method IN [POST,PUT,DELETE,PATCH]) AND (UriPath starts_with '/api/') AND NOT (SingleHeader 'origin' regex_match '^https://app\.example\.com$')
